title: Strings and frets
summary: A guitar makes notes with strings; pressing a string on a fret changes the note.

steps.title: A guitar has six strings
steps.body:
A guitar has six **strings**. Each string makes one note when you pluck it. The thickest string gives the lowest note and the thinnest string gives the highest note.

**Why it matters:** Every guitar instruction your band gives you starts with a string: "play it on the A string". Knowing the strings is the first step to finding any note.

steps.title: The fretboard and its frets
steps.body:
The playing surface along the neck is called the **fretboard**. Thin metal bars cross it, and each bar is a **fret**. When you press a string just behind a fret, the string gets shorter and the note gets higher.

**Why it matters:** Frets are how a guitarist chooses notes. "Third fret" tells you exactly where to put your finger.

steps.title: The open string
steps.body:
When you pluck a string with no finger pressing it, you play an **open string**. It is the lowest note that string can make.

**Why it matters:** Open strings are your starting points and the easiest notes to find. Every other note on that string is counted from it.

steps.title: The six open strings
steps.body: These are the notes of the six open strings, from the thickest to the thinnest. Pluck them one by one and listen to the pitch rise.

items.prompt: Play the lit note. It is the thickest string, played open.
Play the lit note. It is the thinnest string, played open.
Play the lit note. It is the second thickest string, played open.

steps.title: Pluck every string
steps.body: Pluck each string from the thickest to the thinnest and listen. The pitch rises string by string.
